correctness.rationale: A direct two-state generator calculation gives the weighted endpoint Fourier--Laplace resolvent and its invertible positive density g_u(x). The ratio g_u(x)/g_0(x) gives a version of the posterior Laplace transform. Frullani and the I0/I1 Laplace identity yield explicit strictly positive finite measures ν0 and ν1 and exactly the independent compound-Poisson decomposition plus monotone distance coupling. Differentiating these Lévy transforms yields the stated affine mean and variance and e^{-(ρ0+yρ1)} is the exact ballistic atom. The executed packaged Python program independently integrates the source joint Bessel density and the Lévy exponents across four triples and passed 72 numerical comparisons; those checks do not replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The published arXiv:2610.15094v1 provides the entire joint (terminal location,killing time) density, and hence implies all conditional probabilities in principle. The claim deliberately excludes this earlier joint-density result. Its separately derived finite positive Lévy kernels, decomposition as two independent compound-Poisson delays, and endpoint-distance convolution semigroup were not identified in the inspected primary text or the searched relevant mathematical record. Positivity of the Bessel jump kernel and exact finite masses is needed; these are not immediate from Bayes conditioning. Material residual risk: a stronger known result in older resolvent or bridge literature could already express this exact factorization; absence in available searches does not prove novelty.
residual_risks: The source exact joint law trivially determines every conditional distribution; only its explicit independent finite compound-Poisson structure is claimed as an incremental result.
Earlier telegraph resolvent, inverse Gaussian, Bessel bridge, or hitting-time literature may implicitly possess this factorization.
Only abstracts or bibliographic descriptions, not full text, were accessed for Cinque (2022), Ratanov and Kolesnik (2022), and the 2026 first-exit paper.

value.rationale: Endpoint-conditioned travel time is a directly motivated inverse observable for finite-speed random transport. The finite-jump Lévy factorization is structural: it provides constructive posterior sampling rather than generic conditional Bessel densities, monotone coupling in endpoint distance, explicit ballistic probabilities, and affine conditional cumulants. No arbitrary parameter window or unmotivated finite slice is used; this is a natural complete law for all positive model parameters. Its significance remains limited to the symmetric exponentially killed telegraph model.
